headline: PNP Records List 51 Firearms for Sara Duterte, Husband
seoTitle: PNP Records List 51 Firearms for Sara Duterte, Husband | FMB News
seoDescription: PNP records presented in the Sara Duterte impeachment trial list 51 firearms for the vice president and her husband, including four Class A light weapons.
deck: A PNP witness said the couple hold Type 5 collector licences; the court questioned the valuation, and no finding of unlawful possession was made.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Philippine National Police records presented in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial list 51 firearms registered to Duterte and her husband, lawyer Manases “Mans” Carpio, a PNP Firearms and Explosives Office official testified Monday.

Police Maj. Joe Rickson Sangalang, the office’s Records Division chief, said 22 firearms are registered to Duterte and 29 to Carpio. His breakdown included 14 pistols, two revolvers, five rifles and one shotgun for Duterte, and 16 pistols, two revolvers, 10 rifles and one shotgun for Carpio. He said three of Duterte’s rifles and one of Carpio’s were Class A light weapons with fully automatic functions. One firearm registered to Carpio had an expired registration, according to the testimony.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: House prosecutors presented the records under Article II of the impeachment complaint, which alleges unexplained wealth. The prosecution has not established through this testimony alone when the firearms were acquired, what the couple paid for them or whether their acquisition was unlawful.

The PNP’s current-market estimate placed the collection at ₱7,220,370: ₱2,184,550 for Duterte’s firearms and ₱5,035,820 for Carpio’s. The defense stressed that current market prices are not necessarily acquisition costs. Sangalang acknowledged that he had no personal knowledge of what the couple paid.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Sangalang said Duterte and Carpio hold Type 5 licences. Republic Act No. 10591 allows a certified gun collector with that licence to own more than 15 registered firearms, so the number of firearms by itself is not proof of unlawful possession.

Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo called for Congress to review the law after the testimony raised the question of whether a numerical ceiling should apply to collectors. That is a policy proposal, not a change in current law.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Presiding officer Francis Escudero questioned the evidence’s relevance and weight to the unexplained-wealth charge and directed prosecutors to abbreviate the presentation. The defense waived cross-examination after the witness clarified that the ₱7.2-million figure came from a current-market survey, not proof of purchase prices.

The impeachment court will decide what weight, if any, the records carry. As of publication, the testimony had not produced a finding that Duterte or Carpio unlawfully possessed the registered firearms or that the collection constituted unexplained wealth.

verificationNotes: PNA reports the full PNP breakdown of 22 firearms registered to Sara Duterte and 29 to Manases Carpio, the current-market valuation and the defense caveat that the estimate is not proof of acquisition cost.
GMA News independently corroborates the testimony that at least 22 firearms were registered to Duterte and reports the resulting call by Senator Raffy Tulfo for a review of gun-ownership limits.
The official Senate Legislative Reference Bureau text of Republic Act No. 10591 confirms that a Type 5 licence allows a certified gun collector to own more than 15 registered firearms.
The article does not characterize the number of firearms, the presence of Class A light weapons or an expired registration as proof of a criminal violation.
The article attributes the unexplained-wealth theory to House prosecutors and preserves Escudero’s and the defense’s objections concerning relevance and valuation.
Available hearing images were not reused because publication rights were not independently verified. The FMB-owned editorial fallback is used and explicitly labeled non-documentary.
